entry.title: Tokens
entry.summary:
Introduction
Although we interact with LLMs using natural language, these models never processes raw text directly. Before a prompt reaches the model, it is converted into a sequence of tokens, the fundamental units that the model understands. Tokenization is one of the earliest stages of the inference pipeline and influences everything from context windows and API pricing to latency and memory usage. A token is the smallest unit of text processed by a language model, it is not necessarily a word. Depending on the tokenizer, a token may represent: an entire word part of a word punctuation whitespace numbers symbols emojis Different models use different tokenizers, so the same text may be split differently depending on the model. Simply because language models operate on numbers, not text…

entry.summary: "Works on my machine" is one of the oldest jokes in software, and it stopped being funny the first time it cost me a weekend. The code was fine. The environment wasn't. A library version on the build box didn't match production, and nobody could see it because "the environment" was a fuzzy, undocumented thing that lived partly in a config management tool, partly in someone's .bashrc, and partly in tribal memory.
